sections.title: Introduction to AMPS Security
content: Keeping data safe is a critical consideration for production environments.
AMPS provides a robust framework for authentication, entitlement, and data encryption.
Security in AMPS is highly extensible through a plugin-based architecture.

sections.title: Authentication
content: Authentication is the process of assigning and verifying an identity for a connection.
AMPS supports both explicit logon commands and implicit logon (though disabled by default for security).
Once an identity is assigned, it remains for the lifetime of the connection.

sections.title: Entitlements
content: Entitlements enforce permissions to access AMPS resources like topics and admin stats.
Resource types include logon, replication_logon, topic, and admin.
Permissions can be granularly controlled (read, write, replication allowed).

sections.title: Content-Based and Field-Level Security
content: Content-based security uses filters to restrict which records a user can see or publish.
Field-level security uses select lists to hide specific fields from messages.
These features allow for multi-tenant environments on a single AMPS instance.

sections.title: Security Modules
content: AMPS includes several modules: HTTP (RESTful), Multimethod (LDAP/Kerberos), Simple Access, and OAuth.
These modules allow AMPS to integrate with existing enterprise identity providers.
